title: English as a Second Language - Noncredit to Credit Transition

program.section_heading: Certificate of Competency in English as a Second Language - Noncredit to Credit Transition
outcomes: Demonstrate ability to successfully perform in functional life tasks such as finding, applying for, interviewing, and performing in a job; analyzing and discussing current events, news, politics, and topical issues; and speaking with native English speakers.

Deliver an argumentative or informative presentation (4-8 minutes) that includes the use of metaphors, similes, idioms, various word forms (nominal, verbal, adjectival), and common formal speaking conventions.

Construct grammatically accurate sentences using simple, compound, and complex sentence patterns. Write well developed paragraphs in a variety of rhetorical modes (descriptive, process, comparison, cause-effect, opinion) with a clear topic sentence, relevant supporting sentences, and an appropriate concluding sentence.

Write a four to five-paragraph essay with a clear introduction, body, and conclusion using a variety of complex sentences, transition words, and academic writing elements, including a basic thesis statement, topic sentences, claims, and supporting details. Use correct spelling and grammar, proper punctuation and capitalization.
Deduce meanings of new words from the context and through word stem analysis. Demonstrate comprehension of various reading passages
